statements.t: Our primary focus is on constructing and selling single-family homes across entry-level, first-time move-up, second-time move-up and active adult markets, and we also sell homes to third-party investors that intend to lease the homes (“built-for-rent contracts”).
Looking ahead, we do not currently expect near-term relief from these pressures.
Absent a sustained improvement in mortgage rates or overall affordability, we expect homebuyers to remain highly price- and payment-sensitive and competitive incentive activity to remain elevated.

We also expect higher energy, materials and labor costs, and tighter skilled labor availability, including from changes in immigration enforcement, which may extend construction cycle times and which may not be able to be offset through pricing.

Our results are expected to remain sensitive to changes in mortgage rates, consumer confidence, labor market conditions, energy prices, new and resale housing supply and the broader economic environment.

Following the Beazer acquisition, our near-term priorities also include integrating Beazer’s operations, pursuing anticipated operational efficiencies, maintaining disciplined land and inventory investment across the combined platform and managing the combined Company’s capital structure.

Our future results will include Beazer’s operations beginning on October 20, 2026, the acquisition date, and will be affected by transaction and integration costs, purchase accounting adjustments and incremental financing costs.
Ending active community count is an important metric to forecast future net sales for our business.

Our backlog at any given time will be affected by cancellations, the number of our active communities and changes in the percentage of spec home sales versus pre-order sales and built-for-rent contracts, which are customarily delivered over a longer period of time.
Approximately 535 of the homes in our backlog are expected to be delivered in 2027 and beyond.

We believe our focus on delivering quality homes at affordable prices, targeted mortgage buydown programs and sales incentive strategies, along with our focus on spec homes which shorten the time between contract signing and closing, all contribute to our relatively low cancellation rates.
We intend to re-deploy our generated net cash to acquire and control land and further grow our operations year over year.

The majority of our projects begin at the land acquisition and development stage when we enter into finished lot option and land bank option contracts by placing a deposit with a land seller, developer or land banker.
When entering into these contracts, we also agree to purchase finished lots at predetermined prices, time frames and quantities that match our expected selling pace in the communities.
The initial investment and lot option fees require us to have the ability to allocate liquidity resources to projects that will not generate cash inflows or operating income in the near term.
We intend to continue to reinvest our earnings into our business and focus on expanding our operations.

In addition, as the opportunity to purchase finished lots in desired locations becomes increasingly more limited and competitive, we are committed to allocating additional liquidity to land bank deposits on land development projects, as this strategy mitigates the risks associated with holding undeveloped land on our balance sheet, while allowing us to control adequate lot supply in our key markets to support…
We will remain opportunistic while assessing available capital in the debt and equity markets.

Our impairment assessment requires significant estimates and judgments, including projected revenues and margins, and discount rates, which are largely influenced by the current housing market environment.

statements.t: Our third-quarter results include $23 million of one-time transaction costs related to the deal, and we expect additional nonrecurring transaction and integration costs in the fourth quarter.
Beazer is a transformational acquisition for our Company, and we expect to generate significant synergies and earnings with our increased scale as the 6 th largest homebuilder in the United States.
We have a detailed integration plan in place and are extremely focused on achieving our fourth-quarter home closing targets.
Reducing leverage remains a key priority, and we will provide updates on our progress in the coming quarters.

As we evaluate the combined Dream Finders and Beazer land portfolio post-acquisition, we intend to optimize our capital allocation by prioritizing higher margin opportunities and exercising our option to terminate land deals that do not meet our return thresholds.
Accordingly, we anticipate recording deal abandonment charges in the fourth quarter as we take steps to strengthen returns and enhance the long-term performance of the combined Company.
We reiterate our 2026 full-year guidance of approximately 9,250 home closings.”
